title: The Laboratory of Settled Opinions

features.name: the test bench
features.desc-on-touch: A counter where copper and water were held separate long enough to be measured. The measuring instruments have since learned to agree with each other, which is how you know they are wrong.

features.name: the opinion ledger
features.desc-on-touch: Records of water colour, copper dissolution rates, chemical conclusions—each entry contradicts the one before it, yet all are marked 'verified' and 'settled'.

features.name: the copper vessel
features.desc-on-touch: A container that held the experimental water. The copper has aged into new colours each time it is consulted—verdigris that blooms and fades, rust-hues that appear and unmake themselves.

features.name: the settlement observer
features.desc-on-touch: A figure that stands at the edge of the lab, neither scientist nor settler, watching the conclusions harden and soften in the verdigris light. It breathes the copper taste and learns what the water learned.

features.name: the comparison chart
features.desc-on-touch: A grid where water and copper are plotted against time, against temperature, against observation. Each axis shifts when you look away, and the conclusions arrive at different answers every visit.

inscription: where opinion learned to set like copper oxides into certainty, and then began to discolour

file.name: Water_Chemistry_Field_Study_1987_Copper_Creek.txt
file.note: Laboratory notes from a water-quality survey of a creek downstream from old copper workings—the data entries have begun to edit themselves, each page showing different conclusions about what was teste
